newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair would have voted against EU fish quotas.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair would have voted against EU fish quotas.

text.p: British opposition Labour party leader Tony Blair said on Tuesday that he would have instructed a Labour minister to vote against a European Union deal on fishing quotas on Tuesday.
"I certainly would have done that," he said during an interview with Sky television news.
Earlier in the day Britain and France were outvoted when EU fisheries ministers meeting in Luxembourg decided to impose a 30 percent cuts in catches.
Blair said it was extraordinary that the British fisheries minister at the meeting had not raised the issue of quotas.

"What is completely absurd is for the (ruling) Conservatives to bang the table and say 'This is all terrible' and then we find (out)...that they didn't even raise the issue that they now say they want to go to war with the rest of Europe over. That is no way to carry on," Blair said.
The Labour leader said it was important to vote against the deal because British fishermen were not getting a good deal from Europe.

"What we have got to do now is to get the best deal possible for them. That is best done by building alliances and having the credibility to secure the best deal for us, otherwise there are thousands of jobs in the fishing industry that can be lost."
